'''Éva Tardos''' ({{IPA|hu|ˈtɒrdoʃ|lang}}; born 1 October 1957) is a Hungarian [[mathematician]] and the [[Jacob Gould Schurman]] Professor of [[Computer Science]] at [[Cornell University]], known for her work in theoretical computer science.<ref name=Cornell-ACM/> For her work, she has received the [[Fulkerson Prize]] (1988), the [[Dantzig Prize]] (2006), and the [[IEEE John von Neumann Medal]] (2019).<ref name=Cornell-ACM/>

Tardos's research interest is algorithms and algorithmic game theory. Her work focuses on the design and analysis of efficient methods for [[combinatorial optimization]] problems on graphs or networks. She has done some work on network flow algorithms like [[approximation algorithm]]s for [[Network flow (function)|network flows]], cut, and clustering problems. Her recent work focuses on [[algorithmic game theory]] and simple auctions.<ref name=one>{{cite web|title=2019 - Eva Tardos |url=https://www.ieee.org/about/awards/bios/vonneumann-recipients.html#2019%20-%20Eva%20Tardos|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180612211409/https://www.ieee.org/about/awards/bios/vonneumann-recipients.html#2019%20-%20Eva%20Tardos|url-status=dead|archive-date=June 12, 2018|publisher=IEEE Advancing Technology for Humanity|access-date=7 November 2019}}</ref>

==Education and career==
Tardos received her Dipl. Math in 1981 and her Ph.D. 1984 from the [[ELTE Faculty of Sciences|Faculty of Sciences]] of the [[Eötvös Loránd University]] under her advisor [[András Frank]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy |id=39422}}</ref>

She was the Chair of the Department of Computer Science at Cornell from 2006 to 2010, and she is currently serving as the Associate Dean of the [[Cornell Ann S. Bowers College of Computing and Information Science|College of Computing and Information Science]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Biography |date=6 April 2018 |url=https://www.computer.org/profiles/eva-tardos|publisher=IEEE Computer Society|access-date=7 November 2019}}</ref>

She was editor-in-chief of ''[[SIAM Journal on Computing]]'' from 2004 to 2009, and from 2015 until 2021, she was editor-in-chief of the ''[[Journal of the ACM]]'' (''JACM'').<ref name=Cornell-ACM>{{cite web|accessdate=24 June 2025|url=https://cis.cornell.edu/people-acm-%C3%A9va-tardos|title=People of ACM - Éva Tardos|date=June 2022|publisher=Cornell University}}</ref> and is currently the [[Economics]] and [[Computation]] area editor of the ''Journal of the ACM'' as well as on the board of editors of ''[[Theory of Computing]]''.<ref name=TheoryComputing>{{cite web|accessdate=24 June 2025 |url=http://theoryofcomputing.org/editors.html|date=14 May 2025 |title=Theory of Computing Editors|work=[[Theory of Computing]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250425224240/http://theoryofcomputing.org/editors.html|archive-date=25 April 2025}}</ref>

She has co-authored, with [[Jon Kleinberg]], the 2005 textbook ''Algorithm Design'' ({{ISBN|9780321295354}}). Along with being a co-editor of 2007 textbook ''Algorithmic Game Theory,'' working alongside [[Noam Nisan]], [[Tim Roughgarden]], and [[Vijay Vazirani|Vijay V. Vazirani]].<ref>{{Cite web |title= |url=https://www.cs.cornell.edu/~eva/ |website=Cornell}}</ref>

==Honors and awards==
Tardos has been elected to the National Academy of Engineering (2007), the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]], and the [[National Academy of Sciences]] (2013)<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20130501022503/http://www.nasonline.org/news-and-multimedia/news/2013_04_30_NAS_Election.html National Academy of Sciences Members and Foreign Associates Elected], [[National Academy of Sciences]], April 30, 2013.</ref> and the [[American Philosophical Society]] (2020)<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.amphilsoc.org/blog/american-philosophical-society-welcomes-new-members-2020|title=The American Philosophical Society Welcomes New Members for 2020}}</ref>
She is also an [[ACM Fellow]] (since 1998), a Fellow of [[INFORMS]],<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20121019011630/http://www.informs.org/Connect-with-People/Fellows INFORMS Fellow]</ref> and a Fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]] (2013)<ref>[http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 2013-08-25.</ref>
She is the recipient of [[Packard Fellow|Packard]], [[Sloan Research Fellowship|Sloan Foundation]], and [[Guggenheim Fellowship|Guggenheim]] fellowships.<ref>{{cite web|title=Eva Tardos receives EATCS computer science award|url=https://news.cornell.edu/stories/2017/02/eva-tardos-receives-eatcs-computer-science-award|publisher=Cornell Chronicle|date=7 February 2017|access-date=7 November 2019}}</ref>

She is the winner of the [[Fulkerson Prize]] (1988),
the [[Dantzig Prize|George B. Dantzig Prize]] (2006),<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.siam.org/prizes/sponsored/dantzig.php |date=November 30, 2012 |title=SIAM: The George B. Dantzig Prize |access-date=July 15, 2013}}</ref>
the [[Van Wijngaarden Award]] (2011),
the [[Gödel Prize]] (2012)<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.acm.org/press-room/news-releases/2012/goedel-prize-2012 |publisher=[[ACM SIGACT]] |date=May 16, 2012 |title=ACM SIGACT Presents Gödel Prize for Research that Illuminated Effects of Selfish Internet Use |url-status=dead |access-date=July 15, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130718154540/http://www.acm.org/press-room/news-releases/2012/goedel-prize-2012 |archive-date=July 18, 2013 }}</ref>
and the [[EATCS]] Award (2017),<ref>[http://www.eatcs.org/index.php/eatcs-award], EATCS award list, July 11, 2017.</ref>
In 2018, the [[Association for Women in Mathematics]] and [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]] selected her as their annual [[Sonia Kovalevsky]] Lecturer.<ref>{{citation|url=https://sites.google.com/site/awmmath/home/announcements/evatardosnamedawm-siamsoniakovalevskylecturer|title=Éva Tardos named AWM-SIAM Sonia Kovalevsky Lecturer|publisher=[[Association for Women in Mathematics]]|date=April 4, 2018}}</ref>
In 2019 she was awarded the [[IEEE John von Neumann Medal]].<ref name=one />

Tardos was named the ACM Athena Lecturer for 2022-2023, for her "fundamental research contributions to combinatorial optimization, approximation algorithms, and algorithmic game theory, and for dedicated mentoring and service to these communities."<ref name=Athena2022>{{cite web|accessdate=24 June 2025|url=https://awards.acm.org/award-recipients/tardos_3252715
|title=Award Recipient Eva Tardos - ACM Athena Lecturer Award (2022)
|work=Award Recipients|publisher=[[Association for Computing Machinery]]}}</ref><ref name=PressRelease>{{cite press release|url=https://awards.acm.org/binaries/content/assets/press-releases/2022/april/athena-2022.pdf|accessdate=24 June 2025
|title=Éva Tardos named ACM Athena Lecturer for technical and mentoring contributions|location=New York, NY|date=20 April 2022|publisher=Association for Computing Machinery}}</ref>

==Personal==
Tardos is married to [[David Shmoys]], a fellow professor at Cornell. Her younger brother, [[Gábor Tardos]], is a mathematics professor in [[Vienna]].<ref>[http://blog.computationalcomplexity.org/2009/02/baseball-families-and-math-families.html Baseball Families and Math Families], [[William Gasarch]], February 12, 2009.</ref> Her father was {{interlanguage link|Márton Tardos|hu|Tardos Márton}}, a Hungarian economist and politician.<ref name="o705">{{cite web | title=Tardos Márton | website=Országgyűlés | url=https://www.parlament.hu/kepviselo/elet/t059.htm | language=hu }}</ref> Her mother was child psychologist Anna Tardos, and her grandmother was child psychologist [[Emmi Pikler]].<ref name="o705" /><ref name="w153">{{cite web | last=Tardos | first=Anna | title=Anna Tardos, Author at Exchange Press | website=Exchange Press | date=2024-04-24 | url=https://hub.exchangepress.com/author/anna-tardos/ }}</ref>
